rules.title: use of enum variants brings bare variant names into scope
rules.statement: `use pkg.Path.Type.{V1, V2, …};` (capitalised Type) registers each Vi as a bare-name alias resolvable unqualified, AND brings the enum type itself into scope (so both `Type::Vi` and bare `Vi` resolve). The bare variant resolves against any in-scope enum that declares it.

rules.title: brace-group use desugars to per-item wildcard imports
rules.statement: `use pkg.{a, b, c};` (lowercase group head) desugars to wildcard imports `pkg.<head>.a`, `pkg.<head>.b`, `pkg.<head>.c` — bringing each listed package/item into wildcard scope. Distinguished from the enum-variant form by the lowercase first letter of the group head.

rules.title: repeated use of same package warns
rules.statement: A `use pkg;` whose package is already in the module's wildcard import scope is a warning (duplicate import); it is otherwise a no-op.

rules.title: self-import is a no-op
rules.statement: `use P;` where P is the current module's own package is a no-op (own-package symbols always resolve first) and produces a redundancy warning.

rules.title: pub use re-exports a package
rules.statement: `pub use pkg;` registers pkg as a re-export from the current package, making it visible to importers of the current package.

rules.title: structurally identical duplicate items dedup; differing ones error
rules.statement: Two item definitions (struct/union/datatype/enum) sharing the same name in the same package are an error UNLESS their AST sub-trees are structurally equal, in which case the duplicate is silently dropped (ODR-style dedup). Structural equality ignores source-line metadata, so identical items emitted by metaprogramming at different source positions still dedup.
rules.divergence: Logos addition: ODR dedup of metacall-emitted items (Rust has no metacall splice model).

rules.title: item names are visible before their definition (forward references)
rules.statement: Type names (struct, union, datatype, enum) and trait names are registered in a name-collection pass before bodies are collected, so an item may reference a type or trait declared later in the same or another module, and cross-file `impl Trait for X` resolves regardless of file order.

rules.title: cfg-false items do not register their name
rules.statement: A `#[cfg(...)]` predicate is evaluated before name registration; an item whose cfg is false registers no name. This permits the same-name-under-mutually-exclusive-cfg idiom (e.g. cfg(unix)/cfg(windows) structs) without a duplicate-name error.

rules.title: #[datatype]/#[annotation] promote a struct into the datatype pipeline
rules.statement: A struct-syntax item annotated `#[datatype]` or `#[annotation]` is treated as a datatype declaration; `#[zoned]` marks self-relative fields and does NOT promote a struct to a datatype.
rules.divergence: Logos addition: datatype/annotation/zoned attributes (no Rust equivalent).

rules.title: unions share the struct/enum type namespace
rules.statement: Union definitions occupy the same type namespace as structs and enums; a union name conflicts with a struct/enum of the same name, and `type Alias = U;` resolves U as a type.

rules.title: predeclared trait carries its visibility
rules.statement: A trait name predeclared during name-collection carries its declared `pub` visibility, so a cross-package reference resolving before the trait's body is collected sees the correct public/private status.

rules.title: unknown attribute is warned
rules.statement: A top-level user `#[name]` attribute that is neither a builtin attribute, a registered metaprog-handler trigger, nor the name of an `#[annotation]` datatype is a warning (likely typo, missing import, or removed handler).

rules.title: recursive by-value type cycles are rejected
rules.statement: A struct/enum graph that contains a by-value (non-indirected) cycle is an error; recursion through a type of statically unknown/infinite size must be broken by an indirection (e.g. a pointer/box).

rules.title: non-Drop struct of all-Copy fields is automatically Copy
rules.statement: A struct that does not implement Drop and whose every field type is Copy is automatically Copy, without an explicit `impl Copy`.
rules.divergence: A: diverges from Rust, which requires an explicit `#[derive(Copy)]`/`impl Copy`.
rules.uncertainty: Exact DIVERGENCES.md tag not confirmed; promotion logic lives in compute_auto_copy_types outside this unit.

rules.title: supertrait impls must be satisfied
rules.statement: For every `impl Trait for T`, the impls of all of Trait's supertraits for T must also be present (checked order-independently after all impls are collected).

rules.title: trait bounds are validated at the declaration site
rules.statement: Trait bounds written on generic declarations are validated where written: each bound must name a known trait and supply the correct number of trait arguments.

rules.title: unused function type-parameter warns
rules.statement: A function type-parameter that appears nowhere in the function's signature is a warning.

rules.title: Implicit prelude is wildcard-injected into source modules unless opted out
rules.statement: The configured implicit-prelude package is implicitly wildcard-imported into every source-side module loaded for the current compilation, making prelude names resolvable unqualified, EXCEPT: (1) modules loaded from binary archives (their producer already applied its own prelude), (2) the prelude package itself, and (3) any file carrying the inner attribute `#![no_implicit_prelude]`. The injection is deduplicated against an explicit `use` of the same package, and an empty implicit-prelude setting injects nothing. The same injection is applied identically in the metaprog discovery pass and the final pass.
rules.divergence: A6/note — prelude package is Logos's package-model analogue of Rust's std prelude; named injectable package + `#![no_implicit_prelude]` opt-out (Rust-analogous but explicitly package-configured).

rules.title: use pkg from module restricts candidates
rules.statement: `use pkg from <module>;` restricts the candidates of `pkg` to the named module. The `from` keyword is contextual (matched as a bare identifier); a missing/incorrect `from` keyword or a module name matching no loaded module is an error.
rules.divergence: Logos addition: per-import module qualification (no Rust equivalent).
